title: A DM never outlives its session: refused once it ends, unread copies moved to its items

story.i_want_to: be refused, with the items it held and who holds them now, when the session I write to has ended, and have my unread DMs follow its work when it ends
story.so_that: no message waits forever in the inbox of a session that will never read it

rationale: PRD R11: a DM lives as long as its session; when the session ends the server re-sends each unread DM into the thread of every item the session held, one copy per item with its own id, or sweeps it if the session held none; and a DM to an ended session is refused at send time, naming the items it held and their current holders. Today nothing ends: a channel post lives 30 days whoever reads it, and session-message.sh to a gone session fails with exit 5 and the text is lost (claude-config bin/session-message.sh:38-40). Release 3 records the end as holders.ended_at through Holders.end_holder/3 (provided by US-52.13); this story hangs the DM's fate on that one transition.

acceptance_criteria.description: Messages.send/4 to a to_holder_id whose holder has ended_at set stores nothing and returns {:error, {:session_ended, held_items}}, rendered as 409 code session_ended with error.held_items = [{story_id, title, current_holder_id}] and the message 'that session has ended; write to one of its items instead (message_send with story_id)'.

Messages.items_held_by/2 returns the stories of the holder's tenant on which a work-item event log row (story_stage_events.actor_holder_id, release 3) names the holder, each with its current assigned_holder_id, so the list includes items the holder released or handed on before it ended.

Messages.on_holder_ended/3, called inside every transaction that sets holders.ended_at, copies each DM to the holder with attachment_seq above its dm cursor into the thread of every item from items_held_by/2 whose delivery stage is not done or failed: one new row per (DM, item), its own id, the original author and body, idempotency_key resent:<dm_id>:<story_id>, in the original DMs' order.

In the same transaction on_holder_ended/3 deletes every DM to the holder and every channel_cursors row of the holder, so a holder that held no live item leaves no message behind (the unread DMs are swept).
on_holder_ended/3 run a second time for the same holder writes no second copy and deletes nothing more (the resent: idempotency keys collide and are skipped; the DMs are already gone).

A DM send racing the end is either refused with session_ended or stored before the end and then copied by it, never stored after the end: Messages.send/4 locks the recipient holder row FOR SHARE and the end locks it FOR UPDATE.
items_held_by/2 and the 409's held_items never name a story or holder of another tenant.

test_cases.name: DM to an ended holder is refused with its items (ConnCase)
preconditions: holder H1 claimed S1 and released it; H2 now holds S1; H1 holds S2; Holders.end_holder/3 on H1 (US-52.13)
expected_results: 409 session_ended, held_items [{S1, title, H2.id}, {S2, title, nil}] in story order; no row stored

test_cases.name: items_held_by reads the event log, not only the current claim (DataCase)
preconditions: as TC-52.25.1, plus S3 never touched by H1
expected_results: S1 and S2 with their current holders; not S3

test_cases.name: end copies unread DMs to live items and sweeps the rest (DataCase)
preconditions: H1 held S1 (live), S5 (escalated) and S4 (done); DMs d1, d2, d3 to H1; H1 acked d1
steps: read S1's thread, S4's thread, DMs to H1, H1's cursors
expected_results: S1's and S5's threads each gain copies of d2 then d3 with new ids and the original authors; S4 gains nothing; no DM to H1 remains; no cursor of H1 remains

test_cases.name: a holder with no items leaves nothing (DataCase)
preconditions: holder H with two unread DMs and no event-log rows
expected_results: zero DMs to H; no thread message created

test_cases.name: a second end changes nothing (DataCase)
expected_results: S1's thread still holds exactly two copies

test_cases.name: send and end race on the holder row (DataCase, async: false: two committed transactions racing, moduledoc says why)
preconditions: live holder H holding S1; Loopctl.Test.ProductionTopology for a second connection
steps: T1: begin end_holder for H and hold before commit
T2: Messages.send DM to H (blocks on the row lock)
expected_results: T2 answers {:error, {:session_ended, _}}; no DM to H exists; repeating with T2 first: the DM is copied to S1 by T1

test_cases.name: tenant isolation of held items (DataCase)
preconditions: holder HA in tenant A held SA; tenant B
steps: send from tenant B to HA after HA ended
expected_results: []; 422 ownership_rejected (not 409), so tenant B learns nothing

test_cases.name: message_send describes the refusal
expected_results: contains session_ended and held_items and says to write to an item

technical_notes: Hook point: Loopctl.Holders.end_holder/3 and POST /api/v1/holders/:id/end (US-52.13 AC-52.13.7) set ended_at in one transaction; on_holder_ended/3 is a step of that Ecto.Multi. Any other path release 3 adds that sets ended_at (a lease-lapse sweep, US-52.19) calls the same step; the step is the only place a DM is deleted.

Event log: story_stage_events with actor_holder_id (README names table: work-item event log, release 3). Closed stages: done and failed only. Not StageMachine.terminal_stages/0 (lib/loopctl/delivery/stage_machine.ex:646, @terminal ~w(done failed escalated) at :174): an escalated item still has a future holder (PRD section 4, release 5), so its thread gets the copy.

Copies go through Messages.insert/2 (US-52.22) so each gets its thread's next attachment_seq; the idempotency index is the one rebuilt in US-52.23 (tenant_id, agent_id, idempotency_key), keyed on the original author's agent_id.
Lock order: send takes the recipient holders row FOR SHARE before Messages.insert/2's advisory lock; end takes it FOR UPDATE first, then the per-thread advisory locks, so the two never deadlock.

409 session_ended in MessageController operation/2 (US-52.23) and FallbackController; CHANGELOG.md entry. The held_items title comes from stories.title; current_holder_id is stories.assigned_holder_id (US-52.14).
non_goals: Ending holders whose session vanished without an end call: release 3 (US-52.19 sets the lease; its sweep calls the same step).
Moving an item's thread with a move: nothing to do, a thread is attached to the item (release 7's move verb, README names table).

failure_modes.partition: n/a: the end and the copy run in one transaction inside loopctl; a client that lost the end's reply retries and AC-52.25.5 makes the retry a no-op.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.25.3 and AC-52.25.4: the unread DMs become thread rows of live items in the same transaction that sets ended_at, so the end's commit is the only moment a DM changes attachment.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.25.5: copies carry resent:<dm_id>:<story_id> idempotency keys, so a repeated end writes nothing twice.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.25.6: a send slow to reach the holder row waits on the end's row lock and is then refused, never stored on an ended holder.
failure_modes.reach: n/a: runs inside the request or sweep transaction that ends the holder, on whichever node serves it.

definition_of_done: End a test session that held a story and had one unread DM: SELECT count(*) FROM channel_posts WHERE to_holder_id = <holder> returns 0 and the story's thread shows the DM's body with idempotency_key resent:<dm id>:<story id>.
defaults: Items whose delivery stage is done or failed get no copy; escalated items do (owner may change).
The refusal's wording: 'that session has ended; write to one of its items instead (message_send with story_id)'.
